Let's check your situation

Was another vehicle involved?

A third-party claim is made against another driver's insurer. If no other vehicle was involved, read the at-fault steps or WhatsApp us.

Did you exchange particulars?

Try to get the other driver's name, phone number, insurer and vehicle number. If they refused or drove off, note what you can and see the Police report note in step 1.

Do you have the other driver's vehicle number?

The vehicle number is the key detail for a claim. Write it down now. Check your dashcam footage for it.

Do you have photos or dashcam footage?

If it is still safe, take photos of both vehicles, the plates, the damage and the scene. Save your dashcam footage now.

Have you contacted your own insurer?

You still report to your own insurer within 24 hours or by the next working day, even when the other driver is at fault.

How a third-party claim works

We can't promise that the other driver's insurer will accept liability or pay for repairs. Liability and claim acceptance are assessed by the insurers involved.

A third-party claim means you claim your repair costs and related losses from the other driver's insurer, instead of from your own policy.

  • Report the accident to your own insurer first, within 24 hours or by the next working day. Take your vehicle to your insurer's approved reporting centre or authorised workshop.
  • Tell the reporting centre or workshop that you intend to claim against the other party.
  • The other driver's insurer assesses the claim and liability. It may arrange to survey your vehicle.
  • Repairs usually start after the claim is assessed. Ask before you repair, so you don't put your claim at risk.
  • If the other insurer gives you trouble, GIA suggests approaching that insurer directly. Your own insurer can explain the options under your policy.

Questions people ask

Can I claim against the other driver's insurance?

Yes, if the other driver is responsible you can make a third-party claim against their insurer. That insurer assesses liability and the claim; acceptance is not guaranteed.

Do I still report to my own insurer if it's not my fault?

Yes. Report to your own insurer within 24 hours or by the next working day, even when you claim from the other driver's insurer.

Can I repair my car before the third-party claim is approved?

Ask first. The other insurer may want to survey your car, and repairing early can make the claim harder. Some insurers also have policy conditions about the order of claims, so check with yours.
